title: Low-Cost, Volume-Controlled Dipstick Urinalysis for Home-Testing
protocol: Fabricate the base plate using computer-aided design (CAD) software.
Draw a rectangular area with dimensions 2.1641 in x 0.0547 in x 6.3828 in (W x H x L).
Measure the test area on the dipstick to determine through-hole placement.
Add through-holes that mimic the size and position of each test pad.
Draw two raised side ledges measuring 2.1641 in x 0.6797 in (W x L).
Draw a stop using the polyline tool, sized at 0.1172 in by 0.2109 in (W x L), to facilitate alignment.
Select lines for the stop and ledge to make one region using the Region command.
Use the Extrude command to raise the region up to a height of 0.0703 in on each side.
Create notches measuring 0.1895 in by 0.3500 in (W x L) on both ledges for alignment with the box.
Position the notch 0.466 in from the bottom edge of the ledge.
Use the Region command to create a rectangle and set extrusion height at 0.1250 in.
Use the Solid Subtract command, select device, press Enter, select the notch region and press Enter.
Repeat on the other side of the device.
Print the base plate on a 3D printer.
Sand the top face area between the ledges with sandpaper to roughen the surface.
Tape the ledges with adhesive tape.
Spray the base plate with a hydrophobic spray.
Apply several (4-8) coats of the basecoat to the base plate.
Hold the can approximately 8-12 inches away from the base plate when spraying.
Wait 30 minutes before applying the topcoat several times (6-8x).
Allow the base plate to dry for 12 hours before use.
Remove the tape from the ledges.
Fabricate the top plate.
Draw a rectangular area to measure 2.05 in x 5.470 in (W x L) in a CAD software using the polyline tool.
Add a rectangular through-hole slightly larger than the size of the test area of the dipstick.
Place it 0.921 in from the top, 1.165 in from the left, and 1.165 in from the right edges of the top plate.
Draw a second through-hole sized 0.075 in x 3.146 in (W x L) in the top plate.
Place the through-hole 0.236 in from the bottom edge, 1.737 in from the top edge, and 1.162 in from the left and right edges of the top plate.
Cut the top plate from a piece of clear acrylic with a laser cutter.
Wipe off any remaining dust or debris on the cut top plate.
Draw a rectangular area with dimensions 0.247 in x 3.3378 in (W x L) in CAD software using the polyline tool.
Add two circular through-holes with a diameter of 0.127 in approximately 0.073 in from the two edges of the inlet cover, one on either side.
Cut the inlet cover from a piece of clear acrylic with a laser cutter.
Draw a rectangular area measuring 2.771 in x 0.0625 in x 5.000 in (W x H x L) using the polyline tool.
Add through-holes that match the position of each test pad in the test area.

Draw the first 0.105 in square through-hole to overlap with the placement of the first test pad: 1.096 in from the left and right edges of the slide, 0.960 in from the top edge, and 1.681 in from the bottom edge.
Add more through-holes as needed (usually 10 total) for the selected dipstick brand of choice.
Space each next through-hole by measuring the distance between test pads on the dipstick.
Cut the slide from clear acrylic using a laser cutter.
Wipe off any remaining dust or debris from the slide.
Spray the front of the slide with hydrophobic spray.
Apply several coats (6-8x) of basecoat to the slide.
Hold the can approximately 8 -12 inches away from the slide when spraying.
Wait 30 minutes before applying the topcoat several times (8-12x).
Allow the slide to dry for 12 hours before use.
Download a QR code from an online QR code generator and print it on paper with sticky adhesive backing.
Place the QR code 0.17 inches from the right of the first through-hole along the same row as all the through-holes.
Cover the QR code with clear tape and secure it to the slide.
Assemble the inlet and plate sleeve.
Fabricate the inlet by gluing the inlet cover onto the top plate where the inlet hole is located using acrylic cement.
Wait 24-48 hours for the pieces to securely bond.
Spray the back of the top plate with hydrophobic spray once the inlet cover is securely bonded to the top plate.
Hold the spray 8-12 inches away from the top plate.
Wait 30 minutes for the spray to dry.
Apply the topcoat several times (6-8x).
Allow the top plate to dry for 12 hours before use.
Glue the completed top plate to the ledges of the base plate with acrylic cement.
Secure the assembly by applying a clamp to the base plate ledges during drying.
Wait 24-48 hours before using the assembled plate sleeve, as per manufacturer’s instructions.
Download the color chart for the brand of dipstick from the manufacturer’s website.
Open the downloaded file in a graphics editor software.
Open the digital file for the top plate template previously used for the laser cutter in a graphics editor software.
Create the color boxes for the chart sticker by matching color blocks from the manufacturer’s chart using the dropper tool and box shape tool on the top plate template, corresponding to each pad row.
Delete the layers associated with the top plate template.
Draw the two long-sided box pieces in CAD software as rectangles measuring 4.92 in x 6.63 in (W x L).
Add a cut-out centered on the bottom edge of part “a” measuring 0.2 in x 6.11 in (W x L).
Draw the two narrow-sided box pieces in CAD software as rectangles measuring 1.805 in x 6.63 in (W x L).
Draw the box top in CAD software as a rectangle with dimensions 1.805 in x 6.63 in (W x L).

Draw an imaging through-hole on the top measuring 0.74 in x 0.910 in (W x L), positioned 3.17 in from the bottom and 2.53 in from the top, with a distance of 0.65 in from the right edge and 0.42 in from the left edge.
Create interlocking edges on all box sides using an extrusion/intrusion pattern on the long edges measuring 0.135 in by 1.17 in (W x L).
Draw two extrusions on each long edge for every side of the box.
Use the same extrusion/intrusion pattern for the short edges, but with intrusions measuring 0.135 in by 0.460 in (W x L).
Cut five pieces using a laser cutter or print them with a 3D printer.
Use black acrylic for cutting to absorb scattered light during testing.
Add black color construction paper to the box interior if it has a gloss finish to prevent scatter from the flash during image analysis.
Download the UrineTest mobile application from GitHub.
Install the UrineTest app onto a mobile phone.
Launch the UrineTest application in the phone.
Read instructions to change analyte names and reading timings based on manufacturer’s specifications.
Insert new input via the text holder window on the screen.
Assemble various components together.
Insert dipstick into the through-holes underneath the plate sleeve.
Place the plate sleeve inside the box with its notch aligned with the box gap.
Place the slide inside the plate sleeve ensuring its through-holes align with the inlet.
Place the phone on the top of the box with the back-camera lens facing the viewing through-hole.
Check for camera visibility on the phone screen prior to testing.
Align the phone so that the dipstick coincides with the boundaries of the black rectangular overlay on screen.
Click the Start button on the app window to begin the test.
Deposit urine into the inlet hole using a disposable polyethylene transfer pipet containing approximately 0.5 mL of urine.
Push the slide into the plate sleeve until it is stopped by the base plate stop.
Discard urine appropriately after testing.
Clean the plate sleeve and slide with 10% bleach solution.
Rinse the plate sleeve and slide with de-ionized water.
Allow the plate sleeve and slide to dry before additional use.
